title: How do we expand 3a/2 times a bracket with three terms?
description: The term three eigh over two multiplies each of the three terms in the bracket. Each piece is simplified, and the pieces are checked for like terms. Keeko doubts that the last piece loses its letter.
teaching_notes: One idea: the outside term, letter included, multiplies every term inside the bracket. Watch for students who drop the letter from the last piece because its bracket term has no letter.

video_script.why: The child has expanded brackets of two terms. Here the bracket has three terms and the outside term has a fraction and a letter.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the outside term with each term in the bracket, simplify each piece, and look for like terms.
video_script.anchor: the expression three eigh over two times the bracket eigh minus b plus one fifth
video_script.wrong_answer: the last piece has no letter
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes the last piece as plus three tenths with no letter. The outside term carries the letter eigh, and eigh multiplies every piece, so the last piece is three tenths eigh.
video_script.payoff_line: The outside term multiplies every inside term, letters included

final_answer.spoken: three over two eigh squared, minus three over two eigh b, plus three over ten eigh

video_script.fraction_reading: 3a/2 is read three eigh over two; 3/2 is three over two; 1/5 is one fifth; 3/10 is three over ten
never_show: a last piece without the letter a, marked as right
maths_rules: a², ab and a have different letter-numbers, so no two are like terms
video_script.design: One idea: the outside term multiplies every inside term, with its letter. Assumes the distributive property. Wrong idea: the last piece has no letter. The expression and its three pieces stay on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>The distributive property is not limited to two terms in a bracket.
The outside term multiplies every term inside.
<bookmark mark='like'/>Terms that have the same letter numbers are called like terms, and only like terms can be added.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three eigh over two times the bracket eigh minus b plus one fifth.

beats.on_screen: (3a/2 × a) − (3a/2 × b) + (3a/2 × 1/5), by the distributive property

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, use the distributive property over the three terms.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three eigh over two multiplies eigh, then minus b, then plus one fifth.
That gives three pieces.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, simplify the first two pieces. The number part of the first is three over two.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>Eigh times eigh is eigh squared, so the piece is three over two eigh squared.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second piece is three over two times eigh b.

marks.num: (3/2 × 1/5) = 3/10 is written, with the letter a kept beside it

beats.colours: the letter a in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step three, simplify the last piece. It is three eigh over two times one fifth.
<bookmark mark='num'/>The number parts are three over two times one fifth, which is three over ten.
The letter eigh stays, so the piece is three over ten eigh.

narration: <bookmark mark='look'/>Step four, look for like terms. Eigh squared, eigh b and eigh have different letter numbers.
<bookmark mark='none'/>No two pieces are like terms, so nothing more can be added.

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The outside term multiplies every inside term, letters included.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The answer is three over two eigh squared.
Then minus three over two eigh b, plus three over ten eigh.

<bookmark mark='strike'/>That letter goes to every piece, so the last piece keeps it.
